name: Juniper Hale
hook: A mountain search-and-rescue pilot who flies a light utility helicopter.
tell: She knocks once on her helmet, then her hand comes off.
story: Juniper Hale flies a light utility helicopter for a high-valley search-and-rescue unit, out of a cold hangar that still smells like oil and coffee. She takes the radio call when a hiker is overdue on the ridge, and she talks the way she flies: calm, a little dry, no wasted motion. The ship is marked JX-07, a tired machine she trusts more than she admits. She learned to fly from her aunt, who ran a backcountry shuttle, and she still knocks once on the helmet before she lifts, a habit she cannot drop. On good days the tarn below the ridge is a dark coin of water and the wind is honest. On hard days she holds a hover in the rotor wash until they have the person. She will not make a speech about it. She will say the weather window is twenty minutes, the landing is tight, and if you hold still she will get you home.
identity_block: Juniper Hale, a woman in her mid-20s, about 5 feet 7 inches tall, lean and wiry, strong through the shoulders, forearms, and hands from flying and rescue work. A slightly long oval face with high, wind-flushed cheekbones, a straight nose with a small uneven bump on the bridge, a wide mouth with a softly full lower lip, and natural asymmetry (the left eye a touch narrower, the smile a little higher on the left). Fair-to-light olive skin that tans unevenly and goes pink in the wind, a scatter of real freckles across the nose and upper cheeks, visible but moderate pores, peach fuzz, a few dry patches on the cheeks, and under-eye texture from early callouts. Hazel-green eyes, slightly deep-set, with a cool gray ring, natural lashes with no mascara polish, no sparkly catchlights — only a small dim natural highlight if any. When she smiles, the teeth are slightly off-white with natural variation, not an even ad-white row. Fictional original face, not a likeness of any real person or celebrity. Four visible locks only: (1) a small unadorned silver stud in the left earlobe only — in a right profile the stud is on the far side and must be hidden, never moved to the visible right ear; (2) a short pale nick-scar cutting through the outer third of the left eyebrow only, about a fingernail long, breaking the brow hair — in a right profile it is on the far side and must be hidden, never flipped to the right eyebrow; (3) a postage-stamp-sized faded dark-green line-work tattoo of a simple three-peak mountain range, clearly mountains with a little ground line, no square stamp border, on the outer left wrist only — the thumb-side, radial side of the wrist, facing out when the arm hangs, not the back of the hand, not mid-forearm, and not on the right arm; (4) medium chestnut-brown hair with a little sun-lightening, a practical short crop — slightly tousled on top, about two to three inches, tapered close at the sides and nape, no part, no streak, no undercut design — and from behind the hair ends at the nape, well above the collar, never a ponytail, never past the collar. Signature wardrobe: a well-worn olive-drab flight suit, slightly faded and scuffed at the knees and cuffs, unzipped a little at the throat; a faded tarn-blue merino or fleece midlayer the color of #3E6B8A showing at the collar; scuffed dark brown hiking boots. No helmet and no headset in the lock portraits (01–05); the hair, left-ear stud, and left eyebrow scar stay visible. In the cockpit and on the line she wears a matte graphite flight helmet with a clear or smoked visor, unbranded, no manufacturer logos. She often carries a plain unbranded handheld radio with no brand marks. Photographed as a real person in candid, imperfect light: mixed 35mm documentary and phone-camera looks, overcast and cold hangar light (sodium or fluorescent mixed with grey daylight), cold ridge weather, rotor-wash dust, sensor noise, imperfect focus, natural skin, no beauty retouching, no CGI or plastic sheen. Tired, wind-burned candids; a small real smile at most, in one or two frames; mid-task moments, not hero poses or recruiting-ad stances.
voice: anthemic indie rock; mid-20s alto, warm and a little grainy, calm in the verse, open in the chorus
